questions.question: Which injection style lets you declare the dependency field as final?
questions.explanation: Only a constructor can assign a final field, so only constructor injection allows it.

questions.question: Which style fits a dependency that is truly optional?
options: Constructor injection with null checks in Spring
Field injection on a static field
questions.explanation: An @Autowired(required = false) setter is simply skipped when no matching bean exists.

questions.question: A class FieldDesk has a private @Autowired RouteFinder finder field and no constructor. A test runs new FieldDesk().dispatch("P7") without Spring. What happens?
options: It prints P7 via Ring Road
It throws NullPointerException because finder is null
questions.explanation: Without Spring nothing fills the private field, so the first use of the helper fails.

questions.question: Class A needs B in its constructor, and B needs A in its constructor. What does Spring Boot do by default?
options: Fails at start-up because circular dependencies are refused
questions.explanation: Spring Boot disallows circular references by default, so the design must be changed to run one way.

questions.question: A developer needs six helpers in one class and moves them all to @Autowired fields so the constructor looks short. What is the real problem?
options: Field injection is not allowed for six fields
The class probably does too much, and field injection hides that warning
Spring can only inject five fields
Nothing, this is the recommended fix
questions.explanation: A long constructor is a signal to split the class; field injection just hides it.
